entries.description: LIMITATION: fraction of on-node ring-dump (ts,rssi,ch,len,HEX) rows recorded intact at CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_UART_BAUDRATE=115200 under BENCH58 log volume. The ring-dump task and the ESP-IDF log task interleave on the shared UART and bytes are dropped, cutting the hex. Corruption is length-biased (long frames preferentially destroyed), so pcap-derived frame-length histograms and airtime figures from these runs are invalid; intact short metadata lines are the valid evidence source.
entries.formula: clean_rows / total_ring_rows, clean defined as len(hex)/2 == declared_len and no trailing text

entries.description: Over-the-air rejection of forged CEE-PEW frames in Mode C (full stack: FEC + crypto_box + Ed25519 signature). Each forged frame has exactly ONE outer-ciphertext byte corrupted by the one-shot bench forge. Rejection is observed at the crypto_box verify stage with err=CEEPEW_ERR_CRYPTO. Measured by ONE-TO-ONE TIME CORRELATION on the peer device. NOTE: app-level seq accounting must NOT be used (ARQ retransmits a clean copy after each rejected forgery, so every forged seq eventually logs commit err=0) -- see E1-PAIR-METHOD-NOTE.
entries.formula: forged frames with a peer crypto-stage rejection within 2.0 s / forged frames transmitted
entries.value: 16/16 (E1-C) and 16/16 (E2b, independent replicate). Per run: 16 forged frames transmitted, 16 matched to a peer box-stage rejection; E1-C median match latency +0.40 s (max +0.50 s), E2b median 400 ms (range 100-1500 ms); rejection kind box = Discard: crypto_box decrypt FAILED (err=5 = CEEPEW_ERR_CRYPTO); no forged frame reached the application layer.

entries.note: AUDIT: the hand-measured figure in the sealed E1_C RUN_NOTES.md says 2 unexplained rejections; the automated tool (tools/e2_forge_reject.py, device clock, 2.0 s window) reports 3 for E1_C (1 replay @15.2 s, 1 ascon, 1 pipeline) and 6 for E2b. The sealed run was NOT edited - correcting a sealed artifact would break its SHA-256 manifest, so the refinement is recorded here instead. The headline result (16/16 matched, median 400 ms) is identical under both measurements. Tool-verified machine-readable values: E1_C matched_count=16 unmatched_count=0 median_delta_us=400000 max_abs_delta_us=500000; E2b matched_count=16 unmatched_count=0 median_delta_us=400000 max_abs_delta_us=1500000. Both use clock_used=device.

entries.description: METHOD NOTE: app-level per-sequence accept/reject accounting must NOT be used to measure forgery rejection. The one-shot forge plus ARQ retransmission means the corrupted frame is dropped and a CLEAN retry of the same application sequence number is then accepted, so every forged seq eventually logs [BENCHRX] commit seq=N err=0. Only one-to-one time-correlated rejection on the peer device is valid.
entries.value: naive per-seq table reports 8/8 forged accepted (WRONG); time-correlated reports 16/16 rejected (correct)

entries.description: E2(a): can a plain (Mode A) ESP-NOW peer inject into, or establish a session with, a CEE-PEW (Mode C) peer? Two boards 20 cm apart, 300 s, channel 1, hopping off: COM3 = build_cap_plain (Mode A), COM4 = build_cap_ceepew (Mode C). NOTE: the planned criterion (inject 80 campaign frames, count rejects) is UNACHIEVABLE by construction -- BENCH58 TX is gated on session_is_active() AND session_sync_barrier_cleared(), and a mode-mismatched pair cannot clear the barrier, so the gate stops the experiment before injection. Reported instead as handshake-level mutual rejection. n_planned=80 is the planned injection count, NOT this result N.
entries.formula: counts of Discard reject events by stage, per device, over a 300 s dual capture; sessions and application deliveries = 0

entries.description: Root cause of the previously-unexplained E1-A first-cycle post-derive-sync timeout. RESOLVED: the initiator board (DEVICE_A) panicked and rebooted mid-run at host ~14.4-14.5 s, exactly at barrier entry, then had to re-discover and re-pair; the responder stayed in its own barrier until its 30 s timeout expired, so cycle 1 failed and cycle 2 succeeded. NOT an RF, timing, or protocol-barrier defect.
entries.formula: boot/panic markers per device counted across each sealed capture; device boot clocks used for ordering (treated as unsynchronised across boards)
entries.value: DEVICE_A: ble_ctx_lock DEADLOCK (held by pair_supp >2000 ms) x2 -> assert failed xTaskPriorityDisinherit tasks.c:5156 -> Backtrace -> Rebooting / rst:0xc (SW_CPU_RESET), host 14.5 s. DEVICE_B: Post-derive sync timed out after 30000 ms at boot 44170; Received sync byte 0xA5 (HELLO) at boot 59558 = 15.4 s AFTER the timeout. Cycle 2 completed: ACK 0x5A received host 60.1 s. Crash occurred in 1 of 4 captured runs (E1_A only; app_init counts 1x/1x and no backtrace in E1_B, E1_C, E2b).

entries.description: OPEN DEFECT (intermittent): transport_ble BLE context mutex handling can panic the ESP32 and reboot the board during the IDLE-phase entry that immediately precedes the post-derive-sync barrier. The ble_ctx_lock deadlock detector trips when the lock is held by the pair_supp task for >2000 ms, and the following lock timeout leads to a FreeRTOS assertion (xTaskPriorityDisinherit, tasks.c:5156 - disinheriting a mutex not held by the current task). Field symptom: inexplicable ~45 s extra pairing delay followed by success on retry. Observed on the E1-A binary only (1 of 4 captured runs).
entries.value: 1 occurrence in 4 captured runs (E1_A_plain_20261018, DEVICE_A, host 14.5 s)

source.status: PARTIALLY FIXED - the illegal mutex release that produced the panic is removed (see FIX-BLE-CTX-LOCK-RELEASE). The >2 s hold that makes the timeout path reachable, and the 26 call sites that proceed unlocked after a timeout, remain open. Fix not yet built, flashed, or observed on hardware.

entries.description: Fix for BUG-BLE-CTX-LOCK-PANIC. ble_ctx_lock() returns false when its 2 s take times out, but ble_ctx_unlock() called xSemaphoreGive() unconditionally, so a caller that timed out released a mutex it never held. FreeRTOS then attempted to priority-disinherit a mutex the current task did not own, tripping the assertion at tasks.c:5156 and rebooting the board. ble_ctx_unlock() now releases only when the current task is the recorded owner (s_ble_ctx_lock_owner == xTaskGetCurrentTaskHandle()); a timing-out caller becomes a correct no-op.
entries.value: illegal release path removed by construction; NOT yet built, flashed, or reproduced on hardware

source.status: APPLIED AND COMPILE-VERIFIED ONLY - not flashed and not observed on hardware, and the intermittent race cannot be reproduced on demand. All 26 call sites that ignored the false return are now hardened (see FIX-BLE-LOCK-CALLSITE-HARDENING). The separate >2 s hold that made the timeout reachable is addressed by FIX-BLE-ADV-WATCHDOG-LOCK-HOLD.

entries.description: Hardening of the 26 call sites in transport_ble.c that discarded ble_ctx_lock()'s return value and then used g_ble_ctx as if the lock were held. Previously a caller whose 2 s take timed out proceeded into the critical section with no mutual exclusion - a data-corruption defect independent of the panic, and one that would still exist after the crash fix alone. Each site now uses the guarded pattern already present at transport_ble_connect_to_peer: abort the operation with a warning instead of continuing unlocked. The bail value matches each function's return type.
entries.formula: if (!ble_ctx_lock()) { ESP_LOGW(TAG, "<fn>: ble_ctx_lock timed out - skipping"); return <type-appropriate bail>; }
entries.value: 26 sites hardened; the file then has 30 guarded sites and 0 unguarded sites (26 new + the 4 that already checked the return value)

source.status: compile-verified only: ninja exit=0, transport_ble.c.obj rebuilt and newer than its source, image ceepew.bin 0x1573b0 bytes with 31% of the app partition free, brace balance 0. NOT flashed and NOT run on hardware. Caveat: the two state getters now return a conservative default (0U / PAIRING_PHASE_IDLE) when the lock cannot be taken, which is safe but is not equivalent to a successful read - callers treat an unreadable phase as 'not pairing'.

entries.description: Root cause of the >2 s ble_ctx_lock hold that made BUG-BLE-CTX-LOCK-PANIC reachable, found by locating what the holder task actually does while holding the lock. The task named pair_supp is transport_ble_supervisor_task (xTaskCreate at transport_ble.c:4226). Its tick calls transport_ble_supervisor_tick_adv_watchdog(), which took ble_ctx_lock() and then, while still holding it, called transport_ble_start_advertising(). That function reaches the BLE controller synchronously through transport_ble_configure_data_raw_unlocked(): esp_ble_gap_stop_advertising(), esp_ble_gap_config_adv_data_raw() and esp_ble_gap_config_scan_rsp_data_raw() each block until the controller acknowledges. The watchdog only runs when advertising has been down for >=2 s, i.e. precisely when the controller may be unresponsive, so the hold can exceed the 2 s lock timeout - which is what made enter_phase() time out and report the holder as pair_supp. The watchdog now evaluates its condition and updates its state under the lock, releases the lock, and only then performs the re-arm.
entries.formula: lock -> read state, decide need_rearm, update s_adv_down_since_ms -> unlock -> transport_ble_start_advertising()
entries.value: long hold removed from the supervisor/watchdog path; the blocking radio calls now execute with no lock held

source.status: code change applied; compile-verified only. NOT flashed and NOT observed on hardware. The same synchronous-radio-call-under-lock pattern may exist at the other four call sites of transport_ble_start_advertising() (lines 428, 1306, 1798, 3421), which run from GAP/GATTS event handlers - NOT audited here.

entries.description: One-way radio latency (E5), measured with a microsecond sync pulse on a single jumper wire between GPIO14 of both boards (open-drain, assert-low, falling edge timed). The transmitter asserts the line immediately before esp_now_send; the receiver timestamps the edge against its own esp_timer, so both endpoints of the interval lie on the receiver's clock and no cross-board clock correction is used or needed. This is the headline E5 figure.
entries.formula: edge_to_rxcb = t_rxcb - t_edge  (both timestamps on the receiver's own esp_timer_get_time() epoch)

source.status: single bench run, one board pair, 20 cm, channel 1, hopping off, 115200 baud. Medians and IQRs quoted as robust statistics; the DEVICE_B maximum is a stale-latch artifact (see EXP-E5-STALE-EDGE) and is NOT excluded.

entries.description: Transmitter-side stages preceding the sync pulse (E5). submit->pulse is the interval from the campaign submitting frame n to the pulse being asserted (= the on-device cryptographic and ARQ framing path); pulse->sendcb is from the pulse being asserted to the ESP-NOW send callback firing. Both are same-clock intervals on the transmitting board. Reporting these separately is what makes the crypto cost distinguishable from the radio cost.
entries.formula: submit_to_pulse = t_pulse - t_submit ; pulse_to_sendcb = t_sendcb - t_pulse  (same board clock)

source.status: TX sequence coverage is complete and exact on both boards: seq 0..79, unique=80, gaps=0.

entries.description: Receiver-side processing after the ESP-NOW receive callback (E5): rxcb->accept is the interval from frame delivery to the callback to the frame being accepted into the session layer. Consistent with the independently measured Ed25519 verify plus Ascon decrypt cost.

source.status: DEVICE_B maximum is a stale-latch artifact (265880.270 ms), not excluded; median and IQR are robust to it.

entries.description: Measurement limitation in the E5 report that must be disclosed whenever E5 sequence coverage is cited. The RX-side seq field is read from the first byte of the ARQ-decoded frame at the receive-callback hook, which is an internal header byte, NOT the BENCH58 campaign sequence number. It reports a constant 69 on both boards, so the report's RX sequence-coverage lines (unique=1, gaps=0) are void and are not evidence of duplicate or missing frames.
entries.value: RX seq reported as 69..69, unique=1 on both DEVICE_A and DEVICE_B; TX seq valid at 0..79, unique=80, gaps=0

source.status: Does NOT affect the headline edge->rxcb interval: the accept hook reads the same variable within the same process_rx_frame call, so the pairing is self-consistent.

entries.description: Measurement artifact in E5, reported rather than removed. The sync-line ISR latches an edge; if no receive callback consumes it (for example a frame rejected before the callback), the stale latch is consumed by a much later frame, inflating that record's edge->rxcb interval. Affects 1 of 68 DEVICE_B receive records.
entries.value: DEVICE_B edge->rxcb max = 341336.571 ms and rxcb->accept max = 265880.270 ms, both from the same stale-latch mechanism

source.status: NOT excluded - the declared exclusion rule for this run is 'none'. Median and IQR are robust to it. A reviewer must be told the extreme exists.

entries.description: Pre-declared exclusion rule for the E5 run, fixed before analysis so that no post-hoc filtering can flatter the result.
entries.value: none - no frame or record is excluded for being a timing outlier; zero-timestamp records are reported as not-measurable rather than dropped; full distributions including extremes are reported and medians/IQRs are quoted as robust statistics
